calculation.formation_v2: single-phase equilibrium at the phase's low-T composition, 298.15 K; dfS = S - sum x_i S_i(SER); SER entropies from unary equilibria at 298.15 K

mixing_table.partials: H_i - H_i(pure liquid) from central differences of the integral HM_MIX (h = 1e-4)

v2.grid: same composition-set-aware grid as the field map
v2.stability_limits: grid limit snapped to an invariant/congruent/melting T within one grid step, otherwise bisection to 0.01 K at a fixed composition

sentences.text: This synthetic document describes the Ag–Sn binary system as calculated with pycalphad from the SGTE dataset AgSn-12Gie.tdb; every figure, table and stated value is generated, and the exact values are kept in a separate truth key.
The highest invariant reaction, (Ag) + L → ζ, lies at 719 °C.
The Ag–Sn system belongs to the 20 binaries of the ORCHID benchmark, chosen to cover diagram types such as peritectic.
The thermodynamic description is the SGTE collection entry [1], which reproduces the assessment of W. Gierlotka, J. Electron. Mater., 41, 86-108(2012). [2].
The calculations use pycalphad 0.11.2 at 1 atm.
For Ag, the liquidus meets the axis at 962 °C.
For Sn, the liquidus meets the axis at 232 °C.
We obtain 719 °C for the peritectic reaction ((Ag) + L → ζ), where L has x(Sn) = 0.211.
The dataset places a peritectic (ζ + L → Ag3Sn) at 488 °C; the composition of L is a mole fraction of 0.473.
The eutectic reaction L → Ag3Sn + (Sn) is calculated at 220 °C, with L at x(Sn) = 0.961.
Table 1 compares the calculated temperatures with experimental values from the literature [3–5]; in this synthetic document those values and references are fictitious.
According to Table 2, Ag3Sn remains stable up to 488 °C (peritectic).
The solubility of Sn in (Ag) reaches a mole fraction of 0.115 at 719 °C.
At 1300 K the integral mixing enthalpy of the liquid has its minimum, −3.15 kJ/mol, at x(Sn) = 0.220.
The calculated enthalpy of formation of Ag3Sn at 298.15 K is −3.95 kJ/mol per mole of atoms.
Per formula unit Ag3Sn this is −15.8 kJ/mol.
Its heat capacity at room temperature is 25.77 J/(mol K).
For the equiatomic liquid at 1300 K, the Gibbs energy of mixing is −10622 J/mol.
This document is synthetic and exists only to test extraction tools; its truth key lists every boundary, field, invariant, plotted point, table cell and stated value.
